newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi oil being pumped to Turkey - Turk agency.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi oil being pumped to Turkey - Turk agency.

text.p: Iraqi oil began to be pumped to Turkey on Wednesday at around midday local time (1000 GMT), the state-run Anatolian news agency reported.
Around 350,000 bpd of crude is expected to be pumped from the Iraqi oil city of Kirkuk to Turkey's Mediterranean port of Ceyhan, the agency said.

Turkish pipeline officials in Ceyhan confirmed the report. "Yes it has begun, it is here," an official from Turkey's state-run pipeline company Botas told Reuters. He also said 350,000 barrels per day is expected.
Another Botas official said earlier no Iraqi oil was being pumped to Ceyhan because the terminal's tanks had enough crude for the first tanker-load of oil.
He said Iraq had pumped a negligible amount of crude from Kirkuk on Tuesday and halted the process after a few hours for technical reasons.
In Baghdad, an Iraqi oil ministry official said a small technical problem had held up the flow of oil for a short time but Iraqi technicians had solved it very quickly.
